q: A railway servant who has been granted leave on medical certificate shall not be permitted to resume duty on expiry of that leave unless he produces:

options.A: A certificate from his immediate superior that the work requires his presence
options.B: A medical certificate of fitness to resume duty, issued by the competent medical authority
options.C: A written undertaking that he will not apply for leave again for six months
options.D: The sanction of the authority next higher to the leave sanctioning authority

e: Under the Railway Services (Leave) Rules, leave on medical certificate ends only when fitness is certified, so resumption requires a fitness certificate from the competent medical authority, not a superior's note or undertaking.

q: In regard to the grant of leave in continuation of maternity leave to a female railway servant, the correct position is that:

options.A: No leave of any other kind can be granted in continuation of maternity leave
options.B: Leave in continuation can be granted only on production of a medical certificate
options.C: Leave of any kind due and admissible to her may be granted in continuation of maternity leave without production of a medical certificate
options.D: Only Leave on Average Pay can be granted in continuation of maternity leave

e: Leave Rules permit leave of any kind due and admissible to be granted in continuation of maternity leave, and no medical certificate is required for such continuation merely because it follows maternity leave.

q: Where Sundays and other holidays fall within the period of joining time admissible to a railway servant on transfer in public interest, such Sundays and holidays are:

options.A: Counted as part of the joining time admissible to him
options.B: Excluded, and the joining time is extended by the number of such holidays
options.C: Counted only where the journey is performed by rail
options.D: Treated as casual leave debited to his account

e: Under the Joining Time Rules, Sundays and holidays falling within the spell of joining time are counted as part of it; only holidays following the joining time extend it.

q: The position regarding the advance of leave salary to a railway servant proceeding on leave, under the 7th CPC dispensation, is that the advance:

options.A: The leave sanctioned to him is for a period of not less than seven days
options.B: He proceeds on casual leave for his home town
options.C: He has completed twenty years of service
options.D: Stands abolished and is no longer admissible

e: The advance of leave salary was among the advances abolished on the 7th CPC recommendations, so it is no longer admissible to a railway servant proceeding on leave.

q: A railway servant to whom study leave is granted for pursuing a course of study is required, before the leave is granted, to:

options.A: Surrender the railway quarter allotted to him
options.B: Refund the entire cost of his earlier training
options.C: Execute a bond, in the prescribed form, undertaking to serve the Railways on return from study leave, failing which he shall refund the amounts due under the bond
options.D: Resign from his lien in the parent cadre for the period of study

e: Study leave under the Leave Rules is granted only after the railway servant executes a bond in the prescribed form to serve the Railways on return, failing which the amounts due under the bond are refundable.

q: A railway servant who is on leave shall not take up any other service or employment elsewhere during the period of leave unless he has obtained the previous sanction of:

options.A: The Railway Board in all cases
options.B: The authority competent to sanction his leave
options.C: His next below in the cadre
options.D: The Accounts Officer of his unit

e: The Leave Rules bar a railway servant on leave from taking up other service or employment without the previous sanction of the authority competent to sanction his leave.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 23,100 in Level 2 of the Pay Matrix is promoted to a post in Level 3. On fixation of his pay on promotion, after grant of one increment in Level 2, his pay in Level 3 will be fixed at:
e: One increment in Level 2 takes Rs 23,100 to Rs 23,800, and under FR 22 fixation the pay in Level 3 is fixed at the cell equal to, or next above, that figure, which is Rs 23,800.

q: A premature (advance) increment under Fundamental Rule 27 can be granted to a railway servant:

options.A: Freely by his immediate superior for good work
options.B: Automatically on completion of every five years of service
options.C: Only by the Head of Office, without any higher sanction
options.D: Only in exceptional circumstances, with the sanction of the prescribed competent authority

e: FR 27 permits a premature increment only in exceptional circumstances and only with the sanction of the prescribed competent authority; it is never automatic or at a superior's free discretion.

q: A stagnation increment granted to a railway servant who has reached the maximum of his Level is treated as:

options.A: An ex-gratia payment which is not reckoned for any purpose
options.B: An allowance which is not reckoned for pension
options.C: Pay for all purposes, including pensionary benefits
options.D: Personal pay to be absorbed in the next promotion

e: A stagnation increment is granted at the rate of the last increment when pay stagnates at the maximum of the Level, and it is treated as pay for all purposes, including pensionary benefits.

q: The personal pay granted to a railway servant as an incentive for promoting the small family norm, on his undergoing sterilisation operation, is:

options.A: Absorbed against future increases in his pay
options.B: Payable in addition to pay throughout his service without any adjustment
options.C: Converted into a recurring allowance after five years
options.D: Recovered from him at the time of his retirement

e: The special increment for undergoing sterilisation under the small family norm is granted as personal pay which, under the incentive orders (Ministry of Finance OM 7(39)-E.III/79; RBE No. 180/99), is not absorbed in future increases in pay and remains payable in addition to pay throughout service.

q: For the purposes specified in the rules, such as retirement benefits and the like, the pay element reckoned in the running allowance of running staff is:

options.A: 10 per cent of the basic pay of the running staff
options.B: 30 per cent of the basic pay of the running staff
options.C: 55 per cent of the basic pay of the running staff
options.D: The entire kilometreage earned in the month

e: For retirement benefits, 55 per cent of the basic pay of running staff is reckoned as the pay element of running allowance (Running Allowance Rules; RBE No. 85/2019); the 30 per cent element applies to other specified purposes, not to retirement benefits.

q: On the re-employment of an ex-serviceman in a civil post on the Railways, his pay in the re-employed post is ordinarily fixed:

options.A: At the last pay drawn by him in military service
options.B: At the maximum of the scale of the re-employed post
options.C: At the minimum of the scale of the re-employed post, the pension drawn by him for his military service being ignored for the purpose of such fixation in the prescribed cases
options.D: After deducting the full amount of his military pension from the pay of the post

e: On re-employment of an ex-serviceman in a civil post, pay is fixed at the minimum of the scale of the re-employed post, with his military pension ignored for fixation in the prescribed cases.

q: Where a railway servant is appointed, by way of promotion, to another post carrying the same Level in the Pay Matrix as the Level of the post already held by him, the correct position regarding fixation of his pay is that:

options.A: He is granted one increment in the higher Level
options.B: His pay is fixed at the minimum of the new post in all cases
options.C: He gets the benefit of two increments for assuming higher responsibility
options.D: No increment is admissible on such appointment and his pay remains at the same stage, as the appointment does not involve a higher Level

e: Fixation under FR 22 gives an increment only where the new post is in a higher Level; appointment to a post in the same Level carries no increment and pay stays at the same stage.

q: A railway pensioner who retires on superannuation pension and applies for commutation of a portion of his pension within one year of the date of his retirement is entitled to get the commutation:

options.A: Without undergoing a medical examination
options.B: Only after examination by a Medical Board in all cases
options.C: Only if he had also applied before his retirement
options.D: Only up to 20 per cent of his pension without medical examination

e: Under the Railway Services (Pension) Rules, commutation applied for within one year of retirement on superannuation is granted without medical examination; medical examination is needed only for later applications.

q: Where the spouse of a deceased railway servant is charged with the offence of murdering the railway servant, the family pension admissible to that spouse is:

options.A: Paid to the spouse in full, as the charge is not yet proved
options.B: Not payable to the spouse until the spouse is acquitted or discharged of the charge
options.C: Paid to the spouse at half the normal rate during the trial
options.D: Permanently forfeited, even if the spouse is ultimately acquitted

e: The Pension Rules provide that family pension is not payable to a spouse charged with murdering the railway servant until that spouse is acquitted or discharged of the charge.

q: A posthumous child of a deceased railway servant, that is, a child born after the death of the railway servant, is:

options.A: Not treated as a member of the family for any purpose
options.B: Eligible for family pension only after attaining the age of 18 years
options.C: Treated as a member of the family and is eligible for family pension, subject to the prescribed conditions
options.D: Eligible only for gratuity and not for family pension

e: A posthumous child, born after the death of the railway servant, is treated as a member of the family under the Pension Rules and is eligible for family pension subject to the prescribed conditions.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding counting of Extra Ordinary Leave as qualifying service for pension:
1. Extra Ordinary Leave granted on medical certificate counts as qualifying service.
2. Extra Ordinary Leave granted otherwise than on medical certificate counts as qualifying service only where the competent authority orders it to be so counted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: Extra Ordinary Leave on medical certificate counts as qualifying service, and EOL on other grounds counts only where the competent authority specifically orders it to count.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 30 years of qualifying service, that is, 60 completed six-monthly periods. His emoluments at retirement are Rs 88,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of emoluments for each completed six-monthly period, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per completed six-monthly period: Rs 88,000 divided by 4 is Rs 22,000, and Rs 22,000 multiplied by 60 periods gives Rs 13,20,000.

q: A railway servant resigns from service with 120 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His pay at the time of resignation is Rs 60,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him, to the extent of one-half of the leave at his credit, will be:
e: On resignation, cash equivalent is payable for only half the LAP at credit, that is 60 days: pay plus DA is Rs 90,000 a month, so 60 days at one-thirtieth per day gives Rs 1,80,000.

q: Where a railway pensioner dies after having applied for commutation of a portion of his pension, but before receiving the lump sum amount of the commuted value, the correct position is that:

options.A: The commuted value is payable to his family, and is not lost by reason of his death
options.B: The application lapses and no amount is payable to anyone
options.C: The commuted value is payable only to the nominee for gratuity
options.D: The commuted value is credited back to the Government in all cases

e: Under the Commutation Rules, if the applicant dies after applying but before receiving payment, the commuted value remains payable to his family and does not lapse on his death.

q: In regard to subscription to the General Provident Fund by a railway servant during the period of his suspension, the correct position is that:

options.A: Subscription is compulsory at double the normal rate during suspension
options.B: His subscription is recovered by the office even where he does not elect to subscribe
options.C: Subscription during suspension is optional, and the railway servant may elect not to subscribe for that period
options.D: His Provident Fund account is closed for the period of suspension

e: Subscription to the General Provident Fund is suspended during suspension unless the subscriber elects otherwise; subscription during suspension is optional and he may elect not to subscribe.

q: During the course of a year, a subscriber to the General Provident Fund may, in regard to the amount of his monthly subscription:

options.A: Enhance it any number of times without restriction
options.B: Enhance it not more than twice, and reduce it not more than once
options.C: Neither enhance nor reduce it under any circumstances
options.D: Reduce it any number of times, but never enhance it

e: Under the GPF Rules a subscriber may enhance his subscription not more than twice, and reduce it not more than once, during the course of a year.

q: House Rent Allowance admissible to a railway servant at the station of his posting continues to be admissible to him, at the same rate, during a period of leave for the first:

options.A: 30 days of leave only
options.B: 60 days of leave only
options.C: 90 days of leave only
options.D: 180 days of leave

e: HRA at the rate drawn at the station of posting continues during leave for the first 180 days, after which it is regulated under the conditions prescribed for longer leave.

q: Where both husband and wife are railway servants, are posted at the same station and are living together in a rented house, neither of them having been allotted Government accommodation at that station, House Rent Allowance is admissible to:

options.A: Both of them, each being independently entitled to it, subject to the prescribed conditions
options.B: Only the spouse drawing the higher pay
options.C: Only the husband, as a matter of course
options.D: Neither of them, as only one House Rent Allowance is admissible per family

e: Where both spouses are railway servants living together in a rented house with no Government accommodation allotted to either, each is independently entitled to HRA subject to the prescribed conditions.

q: Transport Allowance is NOT admissible to a railway servant for the period during which he remains on leave for a period exceeding:

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 15 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 90 days

e: Transport Allowance is not admissible for the entire month where the railway servant is on leave for a period exceeding 30 days, as he does not attend duty during that period.

q: Split Duty Allowance, admissible under the 7th CPC dispensation, is payable to a railway servant:

options.A: For every day on which he works beyond his rostered hours
options.B: Whose duty at the place of work is split into spells with an intervening break, in the prescribed circumstances
options.C: Who is transferred from one station to another in the middle of the month
options.D: Who shares his duties with another railway servant of the same grade

e: Split Duty Allowance is payable where duty is split into two or more spells with an intervening break at the place of work, in the circumstances prescribed under the 7th CPC dispensation.

q: Allowance in lieu of Kilometreage (ALK) is admissible to running staff for the period during which they are:

options.A: Performing regular running duty on a train
options.B: On casual leave at their headquarters
options.C: Granted Productivity Linked Bonus for the year
options.D: Kept away from running duty and are not allowed to perform running duty, in the circumstances prescribed in the rules

e: Allowance in lieu of Kilometreage is paid to running staff who are kept away from running duty and not allowed to perform it, in place of the kilometreage they would otherwise have earned.

q: The position regarding the advance of pay to a railway servant on his transfer in public interest, under the 7th CPC dispensation, is that the advance:

options.A: Stands abolished and is no longer admissible
options.B: Three months' pay of the railway servant
options.C: Six months' pay of the railway servant
options.D: Fifteen days' pay of the railway servant

e: The advance of pay on transfer was abolished on the 7th CPC recommendations, so no advance of pay is admissible to a railway servant on transfer in public interest.

q: A claim for Travelling Allowance by a railway servant is required to be preferred within the prescribed time limit from the date of completion of the journey, failing which the claim is treated as forfeited. That time limit is:

options.A: 15 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 60 days
options.D: One year

e: Under the Travelling Allowance Rules a TA claim must be preferred within 60 days of completion of the journey, failing which the claim is treated as forfeited.

q: The Productivity Linked Bonus admissible to eligible railway employees is calculated with reference to a monthly wage ceiling of:

options.A: Rs 3,500 per month
options.B: Rs 7,000 per month
options.C: Rs 10,000 per month
options.D: Rs 21,000 per month

e: Productivity Linked Bonus for eligible railway employees is computed with reference to the prescribed monthly wage ceiling of Rs 7,000.

q: Cash Handling and Treasury Allowance, admissible under the 7th CPC dispensation, is payable to:

options.A: Every railway servant who handles sealed cash boxes in transit
options.B: Only to officers of the Accounts Department
options.C: Only to staff working in the Railway Recruitment Boards
options.D: Cashiers and such other staff who are entrusted with the handling and disbursement of cash, with reference to the average monthly amount of cash disbursed by them

e: Cash Handling and Treasury Allowance is payable to cashiers and other staff entrusted with handling and disbursement of cash, graded with reference to the average monthly cash disbursed by them.

q: A railway servant who is placed under suspension is, during the period of suspension:

options.A: Not permitted to leave his headquarters without obtaining the previous permission of the authority which placed him under suspension
options.B: Free to leave his headquarters and reside anywhere in India
options.C: Required to proceed on leave for the entire period of suspension
options.D: Permitted to take up private employment at his place of residence

e: A suspended railway servant remains subject to control and cannot leave his headquarters without the previous permission of the authority which placed him under suspension.

q: The lien of a railway servant on a permanent post held by him substantively is suspended when he:

options.A: Proceeds on Leave on Average Pay for more than 30 days
options.B: Is granted an annual increment in that post
options.C: Is appointed substantively to another permanent post
options.D: Is sent on a training course of three months' duration

e: Lien on a permanent post is suspended when the railway servant is appointed substantively to another permanent post, as he cannot hold lien on two substantive posts at once.

q: The 'catch-up' rule, applied in matters of seniority on the Railways, means that:

options.A: A junior employee is automatically promoted ahead of his senior in every case
options.B: A general category employee who was senior in the lower grade, but is promoted later than a reserved category junior who had been promoted earlier by reservation, regains his seniority over that junior in the higher grade on his promotion
options.C: All promotions by reservation carry consequential seniority without any exception
options.D: Seniority in the higher grade is always counted from the date of the vacancy

e: Under the catch-up rule, a senior general category employee promoted later regains seniority in the higher grade over a reserved category junior who was promoted earlier only through reservation.

q: The periodical restructuring of cadres on the Railways, under which the percentage distribution of posts in the higher grades of a cadre is revised, is normally undertaken at intervals of:

options.A: Every year
options.B: Every two years
options.C: Every ten years
options.D: Every five years

e: Cadre restructuring, which revises the percentage distribution of posts in the higher grades of a cadre, is normally undertaken at intervals of five years.

q: A 'No Demand Certificate', required in connection with the settlement of the dues of a railway servant on his retirement, is a certificate to the effect that:

options.A: No amounts are outstanding against the railway servant towards Government dues, or that the dues outstanding have been noted for recovery
options.B: The railway servant has no demand for promotion in the future
options.C: The family of the railway servant has no claim to family pension
options.D: No post is demanded by the cadre for the next financial year

e: A No Demand Certificate certifies that no Government dues are outstanding against the retiring railway servant, or that dues outstanding have been noted for recovery, so settlement can proceed.

q: An Inquiring Authority or a Presenting Officer appointed in a departmental inquiry under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, who is drawn from outside the office of the charged railway servant in the prescribed cases, may be paid:

options.A: A share of the penalty amount imposed in the case
options.B: Double pay for the period of the inquiry in all cases
options.C: An honorarium at the prescribed rates for the work of inquiry or presentation, as the case may be
options.D: No payment of any kind under any circumstances

e: Inquiring Authorities and Presenting Officers drawn from outside the charged official's office in the prescribed cases may be paid an honorarium at the prescribed rates under the Discipline and Appeal Rules.

q: In a case where it is proposed to impose only a minor penalty on a railway servant, the holding of a formal inquiry in the manner prescribed for major penalties is:

options.A: Obligatory in every minor penalty case
options.B: Not obligatory; such an inquiry is held only where the disciplinary authority considers it necessary, subject to the prescribed exceptions
options.C: Prohibited in all circumstances
options.D: Required to be held by an officer from another Railway in every case

e: For a minor penalty, a formal inquiry in the major-penalty manner is not obligatory; it is held only where the disciplinary authority considers it necessary, subject to the prescribed exceptions.

q: Breakdown Allowance is admissible to running staff when they are detained at a station, or are called upon to proceed, for attending to:

options.A: Their periodical medical examination
options.B: A departmental selection for promotion
options.C: The annual verification of their service records
options.D: Breakdown duties in connection with an accident or a breakdown on the line, in the prescribed circumstances

e: Breakdown Allowance is admissible when staff are detained at a station or called out for breakdown duties connected with an accident or breakdown on the line, in the prescribed circumstances.

q: Railway servants holding sensitive posts, such as posts involving regular dealing with the public or handling of cash and valuables, are subject to:

options.A: Periodical transfer on completion of the prescribed tenure at such a post
options.B: Permanent retention at the same post till retirement
options.C: Transfer only on their own written request
options.D: Promotion automatically on completion of five years at the post

e: Railway servants on sensitive posts involving public dealing or handling of cash and valuables are liable to periodical transfer on completion of the prescribed tenure at such a post.

q: A railway servant who is deployed on election duty, as a presiding officer or polling officer, in connection with an election to Parliament or to a State Legislature is, for the period of such deployment, including the period of training for that duty:

options.A: Treated as absent from duty, and the period is treated as dies non
options.B: Treated as on duty for that period, and not as on leave
options.C: Required to avail the casual leave at his credit for that period
options.D: Required to avail Leave on Average Pay at his credit for that period

e: A railway servant deployed on election duty, including training for it, is treated as on duty for that period under the election duty instructions, and not as absent or on leave.

q: Where promotions to a selection post are made from a panel formed on the basis of a departmental selection, the seniority of the empanelled railway servants in the higher grade is determined with reference to:

options.A: The date on which each of them actually joins the higher post
options.B: The date of birth of the empanelled railway servants
options.C: The length of their casual service before absorption
options.D: Their order of merit/position in the panel, and not by the date of their actual promotion

e: Seniority of empanelled staff in the higher grade follows their order of merit and position in the selection panel, not the date on which each actually joins the higher post.

q: Extension of service of a railway servant beyond the age of superannuation can be granted:

options.A: Freely by the General Manager for any period
options.B: Only in very exceptional circumstances, with the approval of the competent higher authority, in public interest
options.C: Automatically where the railway servant has a clean record of service
options.D: For a period of five years as a matter of course

e: Extension of service beyond superannuation is an exception grantable only in very exceptional circumstances, in public interest, with the approval of the competent higher authority.

q: Where a railway servant is transferred from one station to another purely at his own request, and not in public interest, the correct position regarding Travelling Allowance is that:

options.A: No Travelling Allowance is admissible to him for the journey on such transfer
options.B: Full Travelling Allowance, including Composite Transfer Grant, is admissible to him
options.C: Travelling Allowance is admissible only for his family and not for himself
options.D: Travelling Allowance is admissible at double the normal rates

e: Travelling Allowance on transfer is admissible only for transfers in public interest; on a transfer purely at his own request, no TA is admissible to the railway servant.

q: A retired railway servant who wishes to join the Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme (RELHS) is required to make:

options.A: A monthly contribution for the rest of his life in all cases
options.B: No contribution of any kind at any stage
options.C: A contribution only in the years in which he avails treatment
options.D: A one-time lump sum contribution, at the prescribed rate, for joining the scheme

e: Membership of RELHS requires a one-time lump sum contribution at the prescribed rate; it is not a monthly or treatment-wise contribution.

q: The monthly pay bill of a railway office is prepared primarily on the basis of the statement furnished by the immediate superior or section in-charge, showing the leave, absence, suspension and other duty particulars of each railway servant for the month. This statement is known as the:

options.A: Scale check statement
options.B: Absentee statement
options.C: Last pay certificate
options.D: Cadre check statement

e: The monthly pay bill is prepared from the absentee statement furnished by the immediate superior or section in-charge, showing leave, absence, suspension and duty particulars of each staff member.

q: A certificate certifying that the increment of a railway servant is due and admissible, and indicating whether the period counting for the increment is complete, is required to be appended to:

options.A: The contingent bill of the office for the month
options.B: The travelling allowance bill of the railway servant
options.C: The final settlement bill on his retirement
options.D: The pay bill of the office for the month in which the increment falls due

e: An increment certificate, certifying that the increment is due and admissible and whether the counting period is complete, is appended to the pay bill for the month in which the increment falls due.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 28,700 in Level 4 of the Pay Matrix is promoted to a post in Level 5. On fixation of his pay on promotion, after grant of one increment in Level 4, his pay in Level 5 will be fixed at:
e: One increment in Level 4 takes Rs 28,700 to Rs 29,600, and pay in Level 5 under FR 22 is fixed at the next cell at or above that figure, which is Rs 30,100.

q: In regard to the admissibility of the pay of a higher post to a railway servant, the correct position is that:

options.A: The pay of the higher post is admissible merely because the railway servant looks after the work of that post informally
options.B: The pay of the higher post is admissible even where the railway servant is only asked to hold current charge of its routine duties
options.C: The pay of the higher post is admissible only where the railway servant is formally appointed to officiate in that post and discharges the full duties and responsibilities attached to it
options.D: The pay of the higher post is admissible automatically whenever the higher post remains vacant for more than one month

e: Officiating pay of a higher post is admissible only on formal appointment to officiate in it with full duties and responsibilities; merely holding current charge of routine duties does not earn it.

q: Where a senior railway servant is holding an ex-cadre post and his junior is promoted in the parent cadre, the senior is given a proforma promotion in the parent cadre. In regard to the monetary benefit of such proforma promotion, the correct position is that:

options.A: His pay is fixed notionally with reference to the date of promotion of his junior, but the actual monetary benefit of the higher pay is admissible to him only from the date on which he actually assumes charge of the higher post on return to the parent cadre
options.B: He draws the higher pay in full, in arrears, from the date of promotion of his junior, even while continuing on the ex-cadre post
options.C: No notional fixation of his pay is made at any stage
options.D: The proforma promotion is treated as cancelled if he does not return to the parent cadre within one month

e: In proforma promotion under the next below rule, pay is fixed notionally from the junior's promotion date, but monetary benefit is payable only from actual assumption of charge on return to the cadre.

q: The stage of 'efficiency bar' in a pay level of a railway servant means that:

options.A: Increments beyond that stage are granted automatically along with other increments
options.B: The efficiency bar stage, once prescribed, can never be crossed by any railway servant
options.C: Crossing of the efficiency bar has the effect of a penalty of withholding of increment
options.D: Increments beyond that stage can be drawn only after the railway servant is specifically declared fit to cross the bar, on an assessment of his work and record of service

e: At an efficiency bar stage, increments beyond it are not automatic; the railway servant must be specifically declared fit to cross the bar on an assessment of his work and service record.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, the practice commonly referred to as 'canvassing' by a railway servant is prohibited in that no railway servant shall:

options.A: Apply for leave through the proper channel
options.B: Submit a representation against an adverse remark in his annual performance report
options.C: Bring or attempt to bring any political or other outside influence to bear upon any superior authority to further his interests in respect of matters pertaining to his service
options.D: Join a recognised railway trade union of his category

e: Rule 20 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 prohibits canvassing: bringing political or other outside influence on a superior authority to further one's service interests.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant who becomes insolvent, or who is habitually in debt, is required to:

options.A: Report the fact of his insolvency or indebtedness to the Government through the prescribed channel
options.B: Resign from railway service immediately on becoming insolvent
options.C: Keep the fact concealed from his superior authority in all circumstances
options.D: Surrender his entire provident fund balance to his creditors

e: Under the Conduct Rules, a railway servant who becomes insolvent or is habitually in debt must report that fact to the Government through the prescribed channel.

q: Rule 13A of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, relating to dowry, provides that no railway servant shall:

options.A: Attend the marriage of a relative where gifts are exchanged
options.B: Give or take, or abet the giving or taking of, dowry in connection with his own marriage or the marriage of any member of his family
options.C: Report the demand of dowry made by any person to the police
options.D: Accept any gift whatsoever from his parents at the time of marriage

e: Rule 13A of the Conduct Rules prohibits giving or taking, or abetting the giving or taking of, dowry in connection with one's own marriage or that of any family member.

q: A railway servant to whom a railway quarter has been allotted for his residence is, under the rules governing allotment of railway accommodation:

options.A: Free to sublet the whole quarter to any outsider of his choice
options.B: Free to transfer the allotment in favour of another railway servant on his own authority
options.C: Entitled to retain the quarter even after it is detected that he has sublet it
options.D: Not permitted to sublet the quarter, in whole or in part, to any person, and unauthorised subletting renders the allotment liable to cancellation besides disciplinary action against him

e: Allotment rules prohibit subletting of a railway quarter in whole or part; unauthorised subletting makes the allotment liable to cancellation besides disciplinary action.

q: Recovery of House Building Advance granted to a railway servant is effected from his pay in the manner that:

options.A: The interest is recovered first in 180 instalments and the principal thereafter in 60 instalments
options.B: The entire amount of principal and interest is recovered in a single instalment at retirement
options.C: The principal is recovered first in not more than 180 monthly instalments, and the interest is recovered thereafter in not more than 60 monthly instalments
options.D: The principal and interest are recovered together in a fixed period of 60 instalments in all cases

e: House Building Advance recovery is ordered principal first in not more than 180 monthly instalments, and interest thereafter in not more than 60 monthly instalments.

q: The advance admissible to a railway servant whose property is affected by a natural calamity such as flood, cyclone or earthquake, for repairing or rebuilding the damaged property, is:

options.A: Stands abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation and is no longer admissible
options.B: An interest-bearing advance, admissible up to a maximum of Rs 1,00,000
options.C: An interest-free advance, admissible up to a maximum of Rs 7,500 in all cases
options.D: A non-recoverable grant paid from the Staff Benefit Fund

e: The natural calamity advance for repair or rebuilding of property damaged by flood, cyclone or earthquake was abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation and is no longer admissible.

q: Subscription to the General Provident Fund by a railway servant who is due to retire on superannuation is required to be discontinued during:

options.A: The last one month of his service before the date of superannuation
options.B: The last three months of his service before the date of superannuation
options.C: The last six months of his service before the date of superannuation
options.D: The last twelve months of his service before the date of superannuation

e: GPF subscription must be discontinued during the last three months of service before superannuation, so the closing balance can be settled at retirement.

q: Verification of the qualifying service of a railway servant, for the purpose of pensionary benefits, is required to be undertaken by the Head of Office, and the result intimated to the railway servant, when he:

options.A: Completes five years of service after his initial appointment
options.B: Is promoted to a gazetted post for the first time
options.C: Applies for a final withdrawal from his Provident Fund
options.D: Completes 25 years of service, or is within five years of the date of his retirement, whichever is earlier

e: Verification of qualifying service is undertaken, and the result intimated to the railway servant, when he completes 25 years of service or is within five years of retirement, whichever is earlier.

q: A railway servant is drawing basic pay of Rs 42,300 in Level 6 of the Pay Matrix. The amount of his basic pay on grant of his next annual increment, as per the cells of the Pay Matrix, will be:
e: In Level 6 of the Pay Matrix, the cell next above Rs 42,300 is Rs 43,600, so the next annual increment, granted at the next higher cell, raises his basic pay to Rs 43,600.

q: In regard to the sanction of leave to a railway servant, the fundamental rule position is that:

options.A: Leave cannot be claimed by a railway servant as a matter of right, and the leave sanctioning authority may refuse or revoke leave already granted when the exigencies of public service so require
options.B: Leave, once it falls due, must be granted by the authority as a matter of right in all cases
options.C: Leave sanctioned to a railway servant can never be revoked under any circumstances
options.D: A railway servant is entitled to proceed on leave without any sanction, provided leave is at his credit

e: Leave is not a matter of right under the Leave Rules; the sanctioning authority may refuse or revoke leave already granted when the exigencies of public service so require.

q: Paternity leave admissible to a male railway servant may be availed of by him during the period:

options.A: At any time before the child attains the age of five years
options.B: Beginning 15 days before the date of delivery of his wife and ending six months after that date
options.C: Only during the first 15 days immediately following the date of delivery
options.D: Only after the expiry of the maternity leave of his wife

e: Paternity leave of 15 days may be availed from 15 days before the delivery of the wife up to six months after the date of delivery.

q: Child Care Leave is not ordinarily granted to a railway servant for a spell shorter than:

options.A: One day at a time
options.B: Three days at a time
options.C: Fifteen days at a time
options.D: Five days at a time

e: Child Care Leave is not ordinarily granted for less than five days at a time, which is the prescribed minimum spell for this leave.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding wilful absence of a railway servant from duty:
1. Wilful absence from duty, which is not regularised by the grant of leave, is treated as dies non.
2. Such an interruption in service entails forfeiture of his past service for pensionary purposes, unless the break is condoned by the competent authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: unregularised wilful absence is treated as dies non, and such an interruption forfeits past service for pension unless the break is condoned by the competent authority.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding resignation of a railway servant:
1. Resignation from railway service ordinarily entails forfeiture of his past service, and he is not entitled to pensionary benefits for that service.
2. A resignation tendered, with proper permission, to take up another appointment under the Government is treated as a technical resignation, and in such a case the past service is not forfeited.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: resignation ordinarily forfeits past service, but a technical resignation with permission to take up another Government appointment does not forfeit past service.

q: Where the period of suspension of a railway servant is prolonged beyond the first three months, the amount of subsistence allowance admissible to him may be varied by the competent authority, namely:

options.A: It may be increased by an amount not exceeding 50 per cent of the subsistence allowance admissible during the first three months, if the prolongation is for reasons not directly attributable to the railway servant
options.B: It must be doubled automatically on the expiry of three months of suspension
options.C: It cannot be varied in any manner after it is first sanctioned
options.D: It must be reduced to nil if the suspension continues beyond three months

e: Under FR 53, if suspension is prolonged beyond three months for reasons not directly attributable to the railway servant, subsistence allowance may be increased by up to 50 per cent.

q: Where a railway servant under suspension is reinstated in service, the authority competent to order the reinstatement is required, under the rules, to:

options.A: Treat the entire period of suspension as leave due, in every case without exception
options.B: Recover the whole subsistence allowance paid to him during the period of suspension
options.C: Cancel his seniority in the grade for the period spent under suspension
options.D: Pass a specific order stating whether the period of suspension shall be treated as a period spent on duty for all purposes, and what proportion of pay and allowances, if any, shall be paid to him for that period

e: On reinstatement, FR 54 requires a specific order on whether the suspension period counts as duty for all purposes and what proportion of pay and allowances, if any, is payable for it.

q: In a departmental inquiry under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, where the charged railway servant, after due notice, fails to appear before the Inquiring Authority and does not submit his written statement of defence without sufficient reason, the Inquiring Authority may:

options.A: Drop the charges automatically for want of participation
options.B: Hold the inquiry ex-parte and record the evidence in his absence
options.C: Refer the case to a criminal court for trial
options.D: Impose the penalty of dismissal without recording any evidence

e: Where the charged railway servant fails to appear after due notice without sufficient reason, the Inquiring Authority may hold the inquiry ex-parte and record evidence in his absence.

q: Departmental proceedings instituted against a railway servant while he was in service, in which a penalty could not be imposed before his retirement, are dealt with after his retirement in that:

options.A: The proceedings abate automatically on the date of his retirement
options.B: The proceedings can result in recovery being ordered from his Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity without any limit
options.C: The proceedings are deemed to have continued after his retirement, and a penalty of withholding or withdrawing his pension, in whole or in part, may be imposed where he is found guilty of grave misconduct or negligence, subject to the prescribed procedure
options.D: The proceedings must be transferred to the Central Administrative Tribunal for decision

e: Proceedings begun in service are deemed to continue after retirement, and pension may be withheld or withdrawn, in whole or part, for grave misconduct or negligence, following the prescribed procedure.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 60,000 per month and Dearness Allowance of Rs 30,000 per month. The contribution payable by the Government to his Tier-I account, at 14 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:

options.A: Rs 8,400 per month
options.B: Rs 9,000 per month
options.C: Rs 10,500 per month
options.D: Rs 12,600 per month

e: Government NPS contribution is 14 per cent of basic pay plus DA: 14 per cent of Rs 90,000 (Rs 60,000 plus Rs 30,000) is Rs 12,600 per month.

q: An eligible non-gazetted railway employee is paid Productivity Linked Bonus for a year equivalent to 78 days' wages, computed with reference to the prescribed monthly wage ceiling of Rs 7,000. The amount of bonus payable to him will be:
e: Bonus for 78 days at the Rs 7,000 ceiling is Rs 7,000 divided by 30, multiplied by 78, which works out to Rs 18,200.

q: A railway servant draws emoluments of Rs 45,000 per month. The minimum amount of subscription payable by him to the General Provident Fund, at 6 per cent of his emoluments, will be:

options.A: Rs 450 per month
options.B: Rs 2,700 per month
options.C: Rs 4,500 per month
options.D: Rs 900 per month

e: Minimum GPF subscription is 6 per cent of emoluments: 6 per cent of Rs 45,000 is Rs 2,700 per month.

q: The basic pension of a railway pensioner is Rs 50,000 per month. On his attaining the age of 90 years, the additional quantum of pension admissible to him, at 40 per cent of his basic pension, will be:

options.A: Rs 10,000 per month
options.B: Rs 15,000 per month
options.C: Rs 20,000 per month
options.D: Rs 25,000 per month

e: Additional pension at age 90 is 40 per cent of basic pension: 40 per cent of Rs 50,000 is Rs 20,000 per month.

q: A railway servant draws basic pay of Rs 52,000 per month and Dearness Allowance of Rs 26,000 per month. The rate of Night Duty Allowance admissible to him for each hour of night duty, computed as basic pay plus Dearness Allowance divided by 200, will be:

options.A: Rs 260 per hour
options.B: Rs 335 per hour
options.C: Rs 520 per hour
options.D: Rs 390 per hour

e: Night Duty Allowance per hour is (basic pay plus DA) divided by 200: (Rs 52,000 plus Rs 26,000) divided by 200 is Rs 390 per hour.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding financial upgradation under the Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme:
1. The upgradation is purely personal to the railway servant and does not confer on him the designation, status or seniority of the higher post.
2. The upgradation is granted in the next level in the hierarchy of the Pay Matrix.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: MACPS upgradation is purely personal, conferring no designation, status or seniority of the higher post, and it is granted in the next Level of the Pay Matrix hierarchy.

q: Where both the husband and the wife were railway servants and both die leaving a child behind, the position regarding family pension payable to that child is that:

options.A: Family pension is payable to the child in respect of only one of the parents, at the option of the guardian
options.B: No family pension is payable to the child for either parent, as both parents are deceased
options.C: The child is eligible to draw two family pensions, one in respect of each parent, subject to the prescribed ceiling on the total amount
options.D: The child is eligible only for a single lump sum payment in lieu of family pension

e: Where both parents were railway servants and both die, the child may draw two family pensions, one for each parent, subject to the prescribed ceiling on the total amount.

q: A railway servant whose date of birth is the first day of a month attains the age of superannuation and retires from service with effect from:

options.A: The first day of that very month itself
options.B: The last day of the month following the month of his birth
options.C: The afternoon of his actual date of birth
options.D: The last day of the month preceding the month in which his date of birth falls

e: A railway servant born on the first day of a month retires on the last day of the month preceding his birth month, the rule treating him as attaining superannuation on that preceding day.

q: Promotion of a railway servant in the artisan (workshop and running shed) grades, from one skilled grade to the next higher grade, is made:

options.A: On the basis of seniority-cum-suitability, subject to his passing the prescribed trade test for the higher grade
options.B: On the basis of seniority alone, without any trade test
options.C: Only through a written competitive examination conducted by the Railway Recruitment Board
options.D: Automatically on completion of two years of service in the lower grade

e: Promotion in artisan grades is by seniority-cum-suitability, and the railway servant must also pass the prescribed trade test for the higher skilled grade.

q: A 'work-charged post' on the Railways is a post which is:

options.A: Sanctioned permanently as part of the regular establishment of a division
options.B: Created for the execution of a specific work, is charged to the estimate of that work, and ordinarily lasts only so long as the work for which it is created continues
options.C: Created to accommodate a medically decategorised railway servant
options.D: Held by a casual labourer engaged on daily wages

e: A work-charged post is created for execution of a specific work, is charged to the estimate of that work, and lasts only so long as that work continues.

q: For the creation of a new post on the Railways, the prescribed manpower-planning requirement is that:

options.A: A new post can be created freely, without surrender of any existing post, in all cases
options.B: Two existing posts must be surrendered for every single new post created
options.C: A matching surrender of an existing post or posts of equivalent money value is ordinarily required, and the money value of posts so surrendered is credited in the vacancy bank maintained for this purpose
options.D: The money value of surrendered posts lapses to the Railway Board at the end of the month of surrender

e: Creation of posts ordinarily requires matching surrender of an existing post or posts of equivalent money value, credited to the vacancy bank maintained for this purpose.

q: The assessment of the requirement of additional posts for an activity on the Railways, for the purpose of creation of posts, is ordinarily made with reference to:

options.A: The personal assessment of the branch officer alone, without any prescribed norm
options.B: The number of posts surrendered by the neighbouring division in the previous year
options.C: The total population of the railway colony attached to the unit
options.D: The approved yardsticks or norms prescribed for that activity, supplemented, where necessary, by a work study of the activity

e: Requirement of additional posts is assessed against the approved yardsticks or norms for the activity, supplemented where necessary by a work study of the activity.

q: Under the rule commonly referred to as FR 56(j), the competent authority may retire a railway servant prematurely, in public interest, before he attains the age of superannuation, after giving him:

options.A: Notice of not less than three months, or three months' pay and allowances in lieu of such notice
options.B: Notice of not less than one month, or one month's pay in lieu thereof
options.C: No notice at all, as the order takes effect immediately in all cases
options.D: Notice of not less than six months in every case

e: Premature retirement under FR 56(j) in public interest requires notice of not less than three months, or three months pay and allowances in lieu of notice.

q: The pay of a person appointed by direct recruitment to a post in a level of the Pay Matrix is fixed, on his appointment, at:

options.A: The maximum cell of that level, as an incentive for fresh recruitment
options.B: The first cell, that is, the minimum entry pay, of that level
options.C: Any cell of that level at the discretion of the appointing authority
options.D: The cell equal to the pay he was drawing in his previous private employment

e: A direct recruit is fixed at the first cell, the minimum entry pay, of the Level of the post to which he is appointed in the Pay Matrix.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding counting of leave for the purpose of increment of a railway servant:
1. All leave, other than Extra Ordinary Leave, ordinarily counts for increment in the level from which the railway servant proceeds on leave.
2. Extra Ordinary Leave taken on private affairs does not count for increment, and the date of his next increment is postponed to the extent of such leave.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: leave other than EOL ordinarily counts for increment, while EOL on private affairs does not count and postpones the next increment to that extent.

q: A railway servant who is medically decategorised for the post held by him, but is fit for an alternative post, is absorbed in a suitable alternative appointment after his case is considered and a suitable post is identified by:

options.A: The Railway Recruitment Board of the region
options.B: The medical authority which decategorised him, acting on its own
options.C: The Staff Welfare Inspector of the division alone
options.D: A Screening Committee constituted for the purpose of assessing and absorbing medically decategorised staff in alternative posts

e: Absorption of medically decategorised staff in a suitable alternative post is arranged after consideration by a Screening Committee constituted for that purpose.

q: A person engaged as an apprentice under the Apprentices Act, 1961, for training in a railway establishment is, during the period of his apprenticeship:

options.A: Treated as a trainee who is paid a stipend during training, and not as a railway servant in employment
options.B: Treated as a regular railway servant for all purposes, including pension
options.C: Entitled to count the period of apprenticeship as qualifying service for pension
options.D: Automatically absorbed in a regular post on completion of training, as a matter of right

e: An apprentice under the Apprentices Act, 1961 is a trainee paid a stipend during training and is not a railway servant in employment during apprenticeship.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 24,500 in Level 2 of the Pay Matrix is granted financial upgradation to Level 3 under the Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme. On fixation of his pay on such upgradation, after grant of one increment in Level 2, his pay in Level 3 will be fixed at:
e: One increment in Level 2 takes Rs 24,500 to Rs 25,200, and on MACPS upgradation the pay in Level 3 is fixed at the cell equal to that figure, which is Rs 25,200.

q: Recruitment to non-gazetted posts on the Railways is ordinarily conducted through the agencies that:

options.A: The Railway Recruitment Boards conduct the recruitment for Group 'C' posts, while the Railway Recruitment Cells conduct the recruitment for erstwhile Group 'D', now Level-1, posts
options.B: The Union Public Service Commission conducts the recruitment for all non-gazetted posts
options.C: The Divisional Railway Manager personally conducts the recruitment for all posts in the division
options.D: The Zonal Railway headquarters conducts the recruitment for Level-1 posts through the Railway Recruitment Boards alone

e: Recruitment to Group C non-gazetted posts is conducted by the Railway Recruitment Boards, while Railway Recruitment Cells recruit for erstwhile Group D, now Level-1, posts.

q: In regard to an ad-hoc promotion or ad-hoc appointment of a railway servant to a higher post, the correct position is that:

options.A: The ad-hoc appointment confers on him a right to regular promotion to that post
options.B: The ad-hoc appointment does not confer on him any right to regular promotion, and the period of ad-hoc service does not count for seniority in the higher grade
options.C: The ad-hoc service counts in full for seniority in the higher grade from the date of the ad-hoc promotion
options.D: An ad-hoc promotion can never be terminated before the retirement of the railway servant

e: An ad-hoc promotion confers no right to regular promotion, and ad-hoc service does not count for seniority in the higher grade.

q: A railway servant who is transferred from one Railway to another purely at his own request, and not in public interest, is, on joining the new Railway, placed in the seniority list of his grade in the new unit:

options.A: At the top of the seniority list, because his request has been accepted
options.B: At the position corresponding to his total length of service in the old Railway
options.C: Immediately below the last panelled candidate of the old Railway
options.D: At the bottom of the seniority list of that grade in the new unit, below all the existing railway servants of that grade, irrespective of his length of service in the old Railway

e: A railway servant joining another Railway on his own request transfer is placed at the bottom of the seniority list of that grade in the new unit, below all existing staff of the grade.

q: An appeal by a railway servant against an order imposing a penalty on him under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is required to be submitted within a period of:

options.A: 15 days from the date of the order appealed against
options.B: 30 days from the date of the order appealed against
options.C: 90 days from the date of the order appealed against
options.D: 45 days from the date on which a copy of the order appealed against is delivered to him

e: Under the Discipline and Appeal Rules, an appeal against a penalty order must be submitted within 45 days from the date on which a copy of the order is delivered to the railway servant.

q: The memorandum of charges served on a railway servant for imposing a major penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is issued in the standard form numbered:

options.A: SF-1
options.B: SF-5
options.C: SF-3
options.D: SF-2

e: The memorandum of charges for imposing a major penalty under the Discipline and Appeal Rules is issued in standard form SF-5.

q: An order of suspension made on a railway servant is required to be reviewed by the competent authority before the expiry of:

options.A: 90 days from the date of the order of suspension
options.B: 30 days from the date of the order of suspension
options.C: Six months from the date of the order of suspension
options.D: One year from the date of the order of suspension

e: A suspension order must be reviewed by the competent authority before the expiry of 90 days from the date of the order of suspension.

q: Which one of the following penalties under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is classified as a minor penalty?

options.A: Compulsory retirement from service
options.B: Reduction to a lower stage in the time scale of pay for a specified period
options.C: Withholding of privilege passes and privilege ticket orders admissible to the railway servant
options.D: Dismissal from service, which shall ordinarily be a disqualification for future employment

e: Withholding of privilege passes and PTOs is listed as a minor penalty under Rule 6 of the Discipline and Appeal Rules, unlike compulsory retirement, reduction in scale or dismissal, which are major.

q: A railway servant who is removed from service is sanctioned a compassionate allowance. The pension that would have been admissible to him on retirement on compensation pension is Rs 30,000 per month. The maximum compassionate allowance that can be sanctioned to him is:

options.A: Rs 30,000 per month
options.B: Rs 20,000 per month
options.C: Rs 15,000 per month
options.D: Rs 10,000 per month

e: Compassionate allowance on removal cannot exceed two-thirds of the pension that would have been admissible: two-thirds of Rs 30,000 is Rs 20,000 per month.

q: The commuted portion of the pension of a railway pensioner is restored to him on the expiry of a period of:

options.A: 10 years from the date of commutation
options.B: 12 years from the date of commutation
options.C: The date on which he attains the age of 75 years
options.D: 15 years from the date of commutation of his pension

e: The commuted portion of pension is restored after 15 years from the date of commutation of the pension.

q: Where departmental proceedings against a railway servant are pending on the date of his retirement, the correct position regarding his retirement benefits is that:

options.A: A provisional pension is authorised to him, but his gratuity is withheld until the conclusion of the proceedings
options.B: No pension of any kind can be authorised to him until the proceedings are concluded
options.C: His full pension and gratuity are paid to him and recovered later if he is found guilty
options.D: His pension is permanently forfeited on the date of his retirement itself

e: Where proceedings are pending at retirement, provisional pension is authorised but gratuity is withheld until the conclusion of the proceedings.

q: A railway pensioner drawing pension through a bank is ordinarily required to submit a life certificate, for continuance of his pension, in the month of:

options.A: January every year
options.B: April every year
options.C: November every year
options.D: July every year

e: A pensioner drawing pension through a bank must ordinarily submit his life certificate in November every year for continuance of pension.

q: The basic pension of a railway pensioner is Rs 40,000 per month. On his attaining the age of 80 years, the additional quantum of pension admissible to him, at 20 per cent of his basic pension, will be:

options.A: Rs 12,000 per month
options.B: Rs 8,000 per month
options.C: Rs 16,000 per month
options.D: Rs 4,000 per month

e: Additional pension at age 80 is 20 per cent of basic pension: 20 per cent of Rs 40,000 is Rs 8,000 per month.

q: A railway servant can seek voluntary retirement from service after completion of the prescribed qualifying service by giving a notice to the appointing authority of not less than:

options.A: One month
options.B: 45 days
options.C: Six months
options.D: Three months

e: Voluntary retirement requires notice of not less than three months to the appointing authority after completion of the prescribed qualifying service.
